decisions.statement: A type file is written by a machine rather than composed by an agent.
Every page type stating a type generator is reached.
A page type stating no type generator has no generator run for it.
A generator sits beside its page type as that page type's `type-generator` section.
A generator writes for every page of the page type stating that generator.
A page type is among the pages its own generator writes for.
A generator that is not there is said rather than refusing the landing.
A generator answering to no `generateTypes` function is said rather than refusing.
A generator that breaks is said rather than refusing the landing.
A file already with the body that would be written again is left out.
A body written here is handed to the formatter rather than left for a landing to reformat.
A file that is not there yet is answered as an addition rather than a replacement.
The types are worked out again only where the change could turn what they hold.
What a change could turn is asked of each generator rather than worked out here.
Which page types state a generator is read from the index before the change.
A generator saying nothing about what a change turns is run.
A generator that could not be loaded is run rather than passed over.
A generator saying the change turns nothing writes no type for that change.
A page type is reached through the shadow of the change being judged.
A generator runs off the body the change leaves rather than off the checkout.
What a change could turn is asked of the generator that change leaves rather than the checkout's.
Nothing here refuses a landing.
Nothing here writes a file.
`loadedBy` names a page type, and only one stating a generator is loaded, so nothing declares it.

definition: the types a page type's generator writes for every page of that page type
